Extensive experiments across diverse datasets demonstrate improved visual quality and geometric consistency, with a 2.23 dB higher PSNR on DL3DV and 32.4% lower ATE on Mip-NeRF360 compared to GLD.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

ru.title: Синтез видов через геометрический latent space с глобальной памятью сцены
ru.desc: В работе предложена система GeoVerse для синтеза новых видов сцены из разреженного набора изображений, которая объединяет геометрическую информацию от предобученной 3D foundation модели с прiors появления из видео-генеративной модели. Ключевая идея заключается в выполнении генерации в геометрическом latent space с использованием диффузионной модели и инъекции признаков через ControlNet-подобный адаптер. Для обеспечения согласованности между видовыми точками применяется глобальная пространственная память, которая накапливает наблюдаемое и синтезированное содержимое и переносит целевые ориентиры на общее представление сцены. Экспериментальные результаты показывают значительное улучшение визуального качества и геометрической консистентности по сравнению с существующими методами.

en.title: GeoVerse: Consistent Novel View Synthesis from Sparse Images
en.desc: The paper introduces GeoVerse, a novel framework for synthesizing new views from sparse images while ensuring consistency across different viewpoints. It combines the strengths of geometry-based methods, which maintain the structure of observed scenes, with video generative models that provide rich appearance information. By utilizing a pretrained 3D foundation model and a ControlNet-style adapter, GeoVerse enhances the completion of unseen regions with learned appearance priors. The framework also incorporates a global spatial memory to ensure coherence between observed and generated content, resulting in improved visual quality and geometric accuracy.

zh.title: GeoVerse：合成一致性新视角的创新框架
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为GeoVerse的新框架，用于从稀疏图像合成新视角图像。该框架结合了几何潜在空间和视频生成模型的外观先验，以实现世界一致性的合成。GeoVerse通过控制网络风格的适配器将多层特征注入几何潜在扩散模型，从而增强结构的完整性。实验结果表明，GeoVerse在视觉质量和几何一致性方面均有显著提升。

papers.title: Fewer Tokens, More Self-Teaching: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Extreme Visual Token Reduction
papers.abstract: Abstract  Visual token reduction is an effective way to accelerate multimodal large language models (MLLMs), but performance deteriorates rapidly under extremely low token budgets. Existing work has explored both visual-token selection and training-based adaptation to reduced visual inputs. We take a step further by asking how a heavily compressed MLLM should learn from the states induced by its own generations. This setting naturally calls for on-policy self-distillation: a heavily compressed model is supervised on the states induced by its own generations, while its full-token counterpart serves as an information-rich teacher. Based on this insight, we propose LT-OPD, a training framework for extreme visual-token reduction. The student rolls out responses with only a small fraction of visual tokens, and a frozen full-token copy of the same MLLM provides distributional supervision along these student-generated trajectories. To stabilize on-policy learning when visual evidence is severely limited, we further introduce a budget-level curriculum that progressively decreases the token budget during training. Across nine benchmarks on Qwen3.5-4B, LT-OPD raises average retained performance under 5% visual-token retention from 68.6% to 82.3%, outperforming training-free, training-based, and reinforcement-learning baselines at the same budget. The gains transfer consistently to Qwen3.5-9B, GLM-4.6V-9B, and LLaVA-OV-1.5-4B. LT-OPD also reduces KV-cache usage by 85.2% and prefill FLOPs by 85.4% without additional inference overhead, demonstrating that on-policy learning can substantially recover capabilities lost to extreme visual-token reduction.

ru.title: На-politique самодистилляция для экстремального сжатия визуальных токенов в мультимодальных моделях
ru.desc: Исследование посвящено ускорению мультимодальных больших языковых моделей через экстремальное сокращение визуальных токенов. Авторы предлагают LT-OPD — фреймворк для обучения сжатой модели на основе на-politique самодистилляции, где сжатая модель учится на состояниях, порождённых её собственными ответами, при помощи полной модели в качестве учителя. Для стабилизации обучения при критическом дефиците визуальной информации применяется curriculum learning, постепенно снижающий бюджет токенов во время тренировки. Метод достигает восстановления 82.3% производительности при сохранении всего 5% визуальных токенов и одновременно снижает потребление памяти KV-cache на 85.2% и вычисления prefill на 85.4% без дополнительных расходов на инференс.

en.title: Boosting MLLM Performance with Smart Token Reduction
en.desc: This paper introduces LT-OPD, a novel training framework designed to enhance the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) under extreme visual-token reduction. It employs on-policy self-distillation, where a compressed model learns from its own generated states while being guided by a full-token model acting as a teacher. The framework also incorporates a budget-level curriculum that gradually decreases the token budget during training, stabilizing the learning process. Experimental results show that LT-OPD significantly improves performance and reduces computational costs compared to existing methods, making it a promising approach for efficient MLLM training.

zh.title: 极限视觉标记减少的自我蒸馏学习
zh.desc: 视觉标记减少是一种加速多模态大型语言模型（MLLMs）的方法，但在极低的标记预算下性能会迅速下降。本文提出了一种新的训练框架LT-OPD，通过自我蒸馏的方式，让压缩后的模型从自身生成的状态中学习，同时利用完整标记的模型作为信息丰富的教师。我们还引入了预算级课程，逐步减少训练过程中的标记预算，以稳定在视觉证据严重有限时的学习。实验结果表明，LT-OPD在多个基准测试中显著提高了在极低视觉标记保留下的平均性能。

papers.title: RenderRank: Learning to Rerank Text with Compressed Visual Tokens
papers.abstract: Abstract  Rendering document text as images allows vision-language models to encode documents as visual tokens, which can reduce input sequence length compared with text input. This reduction in input length is particularly useful for reranking, where each query involves scoring multiple candidate documents and token savings apply to each candidate evaluation. We introduce RenderRank, a reranker that learns query-dependent relevance scoring from compressed visual document representations instead of the text token sequences used by conventional text-based rerankers. Training first aligns relevance scores from visual inputs with those of a text-based teacher, then refines the relative scores of positive and negative documents for the same query. Across 11 datasets from BEIR, RenderRank uses 16.5-35.5% fewer input tokens while achieving an average NDCG@10 of 55.96, outperforming all evaluated text-based baselines below 4B parameters and some larger models. Across four long-document datasets, it achieves an average NDCG@10 of 88.27 with approximately half the average input token count of the evaluated text-based rerankers. In this setting, RenderRank delivers 1.70x the highest average throughput of the evaluated baselines. These results demonstrate that compressed visual representations can support accurate document relevance scoring, providing an alternative to text token representations for reranking.

ru.title: Визуальная компрессия документов для быстрого переранжирования
ru.desc: В статье предлагается RenderRank — переранжировщик документов, который использует визуальные представления текста вместо текстовых токенов для оценки релевантности. Метод изучает выдачу релевантных документов, преобразуя их в изображения и кодируя сжатые визуальные токены через vision-language модель. Обучение происходит в два этапа: выравнивание оценок релевантности с учителем на основе текста и последующая оптимизация различия между релевантными и нерелевантными документами. Решение достигает лучших результатов среди малых моделей, использует на 16-35% меньше токенов и обеспечивает в 1.7 раза выше пропускную способность по сравнению с текстовыми методами.

en.title: Visual Reranking: Less Input, More Accuracy!
en.desc: This paper presents RenderRank, a novel reranking model that utilizes visual representations of documents instead of traditional text tokens. By converting document text into images, RenderRank significantly reduces the number of input tokens needed for processing, which is beneficial for evaluating multiple candidate documents. The model learns to score relevance based on visual inputs by first aligning its scores with those from a text-based teacher and then refining them for better accuracy. The results show that RenderRank not only uses fewer tokens but also achieves higher performance metrics compared to existing text-based rerankers, demonstrating the effectiveness of visual document representations in machine learning tasks.

zh.title: RenderRank：视觉文档重排序的新方法
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为RenderRank的重排序模型，它通过将文档文本渲染为图像来减少输入序列的长度。这种方法特别适用于重排序任务，因为每个查询需要对多个候选文档进行评分，从而节省了每个候选评估的令牌数量。RenderRank通过学习从压缩的视觉文档表示中获取查询相关性评分，而不是传统文本基础的重排序模型使用的文本令牌序列。实验结果表明，RenderRank在多个数据集上表现优异，使用更少的输入令牌同时实现了更高的准确性。

papers.title: Rethinking Automated Voice Similarity by Shifting from EER to Embedding Geometry
papers.abstract: Abstract  Speaker verification (SV) models are commonly assumed to better capture nuances among speaker characteristics as verification accuracy improves, leading to their widespread use as automated proxies for human voice similarity in speech generation tasks. However, by establishing a human perceptual alignment metric and conducting systematic analysis, we demonstrate that perceptual alignment is governed far more by how a model is trained (its learning objective) than by how well it performs (EER). Notably, standard margin-based classification losses (e.g., AAM-Softmax) yield substantially lower perceptual alignment than prototypical metric losses, while EER itself fails to track human judgment, directly challenging the community's implicit assumption. We trace this divergence to embedding geometry, where a model's effective dimensionality (d_{eff}) tracks perceptual alignment with a -0.95 rank correlation, revealing that the dimensional spread favored by classification losses fundamentally clashes with the low-dimensional nature of human voice perception. Imposing a dimensionality bottleneck compresses d_{eff} and raises perceptual alignment (ρ_{align}) from 0.08 to 0.74, establishing a principled geometric criterion for evaluating voice similarity.
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence Center of Research Excellence (NTU AI-CoRE)

ru.title: Геометрия эмбеддингов определяет восприятие голоса больше, чем точность модели
ru.desc: В статье исследуется несоответствие между точностью моделей верификации диктора (метрика EER) и соответствием человеческому восприятию голоса. Авторы показывают, что функция потерь при обучении модели оказывает гораздо большее влияние на согласованность с человеческим суждением, чем качество классификации. Они обнаруживают, что разница в выравнивании с восприятием объясняется геометрией эмбеддингов: эффективная размерность пространства признаков имеет сильную отрицательную корреляцию с перцептивным выравниванием. Применение ограничения на размерность пространства эмбеддингов значительно улучшает соответствие модели человеческому восприятию голоса.

en.title: Training Matters: Aligning Models with Human Voice Perception
en.desc: This paper investigates how speaker verification (SV) models relate to human perception of voice similarity. It reveals that the way a model is trained, particularly its learning objective, has a greater impact on perceptual alignment than its verification accuracy, measured by Equal Error Rate (EER). The study shows that traditional classification losses lead to lower perceptual alignment compared to metric losses, and that the geometry of embeddings plays a crucial role in this relationship. By constraining the dimensionality of the model, the authors improve perceptual alignment significantly, providing a new way to assess voice similarity.

zh.title: 优化模型训练以提升声音相似性评估
zh.desc: 这篇论文探讨了说话人验证模型在捕捉说话人特征细微差别方面的有效性。研究表明，模型的训练目标对感知对齐的影响远大于其性能表现。标准的基于边际的分类损失（如AAM-Softmax）在感知对齐方面表现较差，而原型度量损失则表现更好。通过限制模型的有效维度，可以显著提高感知对齐度，从而为评估声音相似性提供了一个几何标准。

papers.title: Relic: From Multi-Agent Collaboration to Persistent Organizational Capability
papers.abstract: Abstract  Multiple agents may often conflict in an organization: for example, one coding agent changes an interface in a repository, but another continues to develop on the old version where existing tests become stale. A conversation can resolve the episode, but when the participants change, what makes the lesson continue to govern the team? We introduce Relic, which turns recurring collaboration failures into organization-owned, executable protocols. Members reflect on visible work, propose rules, and govern their adoption. Adopted protocols bind triggers, responsibilities, required evidence, and execution consequences to the runtime, while remaining open to revision and retirement. In one traced case, repeated integration friction produces an interface-review rule that governs later pull requests and is revised as work continues. Across 360 controlled runs over ten software workloads and three models, Relic raises complete-contract delivery from 14.06% to 19.76% (+5.71 percentage points) over a matched structured team without the protocol lifecycle, improving all four verified production endpoints in every model stratum. Under fresh-member transfer, behavioral correctness is 25.4% with no inherited protocol, 34.6% with the same rules provided as readable text, and 41.2% with executable bindings, a +6.5-point advantage over text alone. On the full CooperBench benchmark, after excluding broken benchmark pairs, Relic achieves 367/477 (76.9%), establishing the best reported result among peer-structured systems. On the fixed 48-pair same-model subset, Relic also exceeds Solo (29/48 vs. 26/48), reversing the coordination loss exhibited by the official peer baseline. Together, these results show how collaboration experience can become persistent organizational state that remains useful beyond the members who created it.

ru.title: Превращение опыта сотрудничества в постоянные организационные протоколы
ru.desc: В статье представлена система Relic, которая преобразует повторяющиеся ошибки сотрудничества между агентами в организации в исполняемые протоколы, принадлежащие организации. Система позволяет членам команды анализировать видимую работу, предлагать правила и управлять их внедрением, связывая триггеры, ответственность, требуемые доказательства и последствия выполнения с рантаймом. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что Relic увеличивает успешную доставку контрактов с 14.06% до 19.76% и достигает лучших показателей при передаче протоколов новым членам команды. Подход демонстрирует, что опыт сотрудничества может стать постоянным состоянием организации, остающимся полезным даже после того, как члены команды, создавшие эти протоколы, покинут проект.

en.title: Transforming Collaboration Failures into Lasting Protocols
en.desc: This paper presents Relic, a system designed to transform recurring collaboration failures among agents in an organization into executable protocols that can be adopted by the team. By allowing team members to reflect on their work and propose rules, Relic creates a structured approach to govern collaboration, binding responsibilities and consequences to specific actions. The study demonstrates that using Relic significantly improves contract delivery rates and behavioral correctness in software development tasks, especially when protocols are executable rather than just documented. Overall, Relic shows how lessons learned from collaboration can be institutionalized, benefiting future team members and enhancing overall productivity.

zh.title: 将协作经验转化为持久的组织协议
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为Relic的系统，旨在解决组织中多代理之间的协作冲突。Relic将重复出现的协作失败转化为可执行的组织协议，帮助团队成员反思可见的工作并提出规则。通过绑定触发器、责任和执行后果，Relic确保这些协议在运行时有效，并且可以随时修订或废除。实验结果表明，Relic显著提高了团队的交付效率和行为正确性，展示了协作经验如何转化为持久的组织状态。

papers.title: Measuring Collapse and Correction in Homogeneous-Panel LLM Debate
papers.abstract: Abstract  Multi-agent large language model (LLM) debate is often evaluated by whether final answers improve, but movement is not necessarily improvement: the same discussion can rescue an initially wrong majority or destroy an initially correct one. Standard final-accuracy evaluations conflate these opposing mechanisms. We introduce an auditable protocol for homogeneous debate on multiple-choice questions (MCQs) that records each run as a transition ledger over collapse, correction, onset, and signed intervention utility. On 6,925 MMLU-Pro debates, the protocol identifies 253 collapses and a parallel correction ledger that changes how interventions should be judged. Replay experiments reveal the central tradeoff: a leave-one-model-out probe-gated freeze prevents 29 collapses but loses 108 corrections under equal weights, so collapse prevention alone can recommend the wrong policy. A compact pre-debate 8-probe screen is a triage signal: its unadjusted family-level association with conditional-collapse risk is high (G=7, Spearman rho=0.893, exact two-sided p=0.0123), but initial-majority accuracy is a close comparator (rho=0.821; family partial rho=0.767, p=0.0877), so we do not treat it as calibrated or capability-adjusted prediction. Round-level traces localize many collapses to the first debate round, where early disagreement can precede both harmful cascades and useful recovery. We release replayable schemas, coders, audits, cost cards, and zero-API rebuild scripts so future model-scaffold rows can be compared under the same denominators and signed utility ledger.

ru.title: Скрытые механизмы дебата между моделями: от улучшения результата к разрушению истины
ru.desc: В работе исследуется дебат между несколькими LLM-агентами при решении задач множественного выбора, выявляя, что улучшение финального ответа может происходить из-за разных механизмов - исправления ошибок или падения правильного решения. Авторы предложили аудируемый протокол оценки, который отслеживает каждый дебат как цепь переходов между четырьмя состояниями и вычисляет подписанную полезность вмешательств. На датасете MMLU-Pro обнаружены 253 случая падения, и анализ показал компромисс между предотвращением катастрофических ошибок и сохранением исправлений - часто эти цели противоречат друг другу. Исследование предоставляет воспроизводимые схемы, инструменты аудита и результаты для сравнения различных конфигураций LLM-систем под одинаковыми метриками.

en.title: Improving Debate Evaluation in Multi-Agent LLMs
en.desc: This paper discusses the evaluation of multi-agent large language model (LLM) debates, highlighting that simply measuring final answers can be misleading. It introduces a new protocol that tracks the process of debate through a transition ledger, allowing for a clearer understanding of when answers improve or worsen. The study analyzes 6,925 debates and identifies key moments of collapse and correction, revealing a tradeoff between preventing collapses and allowing for necessary corrections. The authors provide tools for future research to ensure consistent evaluation of model performance in debates.

zh.title: 多智能体辩论：评估进步的新方法
zh.desc: 本文探讨了多智能体大型语言模型（LLM）辩论的评估方法，指出最终答案的改善并不一定代表真正的进步。我们提出了一种可审计的协议，用于记录多项选择题（MCQ）辩论的每个过程，包括崩溃、纠正和干预的效用。通过对6925场辩论的分析，我们发现了253次崩溃，并提出了新的干预评估标准。研究表明，早期的分歧可能导致有害的连锁反应或有益的恢复，因此我们提供了可重放的方案和工具，以便未来的模型可以在相同的标准下进行比较。

papers.title: WaveFront Decoding: Parallelized Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Looped language models repeatedly apply a weight-shared block to increase effective depth without increasing parameter count, but the resulting T sequential recurrent-block calls per generated token substantially increase decoding latency. To address the issue, we introduce Wavefront Decoding (WFD), a training-free self-speculative decoding framework designed for looped language models. WFD exploits two properties of these architectures: intermediate recurrence outputs provide effective draft predictions, and weight sharing allows token states at different positions and recurrence depths to be processed in one batched recurrent-block call. WFD organizes these mixed-depth states into a diagonal wavefront, continuously drafting new positions at shallow depth while advancing earlier positions toward full-depth verification. Unlike the phase-separated draft-then-verify schedule, WFD therefore concurrently batches drafting and verification within the same recurrent calls, while rejected drafts are corrected using full-depth predictions. Across six Spec-Bench task categories, WFD achieves 2.42x speedup on Ouro-2.6B and 3.54x on Huginn-3.5B over autoregressive decoding, consistently outperforming draft-then-verify. Cross-recurrence KV sharing further reduces wavefront KV traffic and increases WFD's speedup to 4.81x on Huginn-3.5B. The code is available at https://github.com/summerbro-hhj/wavefront-decoding.

ru.title: Волновое декодирование: конкурентная спекулятивная генерация для циклических языковых моделей
ru.desc: В статье предлагается метод Wavefront Decoding для ускорения декодирования циклических языковых моделей, которые многократно применяют блок с общими весами для увеличения глубины сети без роста числа параметров. Авторы используют самоспекулятивное декодирование, которое эксплуатирует два свойства этих архитектур: промежуточные выходы рекуррентных блоков служат хорошими предсказаниями-кандидатами, а общие веса позволяют обрабатывать состояния токенов на разных позициях и глубинах одновременно. Метод организует состояния смешанной глубины в диагональный волновой фронт, одновременно генерируя новые позиции на мелкой глубине и проверяя ранние позиции на полной глубине, что позволяет избежать разделения на фазы черновика и верификации. На базе моделей размером 2.6B и 3.5B параметров метод достигает ускорения в 2.42-4.81x раз по сравнению с автрегрессивным декодированием, значительно превосходя стандартный подход черновик-затем-проверка.

en.title: Speeding Up Language Models with Wavefront Decoding
en.desc: This paper presents Wavefront Decoding (WFD), a new method to improve the efficiency of looped language models during text generation. WFD allows for faster decoding by batching the processing of token states at different depths, which reduces the time taken for generating each token. It leverages intermediate outputs as draft predictions and corrects them using full-depth predictions, enabling concurrent drafting and verification. The results show significant speed improvements over traditional methods, making WFD a promising approach for enhancing the performance of language models.

zh.title: 波前解码：提升循环语言模型的解码速度
zh.desc: 这篇论文介绍了一种新的解码框架，称为波前解码（WFD），旨在提高循环语言模型的解码速度。WFD利用了循环模型的两个特性：中间递归输出可以提供有效的草稿预测，而权重共享允许在一次批量递归调用中处理不同位置和递归深度的令牌状态。通过将这些混合深度状态组织成对角波前，WFD能够在推进早期位置进行全面深度验证的同时，持续草拟新的浅层位置。实验结果表明，WFD在多个任务上显著提高了解码速度，优于传统的草拟-验证方法。

papers.title: Beyond Timestamps: Decision-Aligned On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) often relies on sparse outcome rewards, providing coarse supervision for long-horizon agents. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this signal with dense privileged feedback. However, we identify Decision--Timestamp Mismatch: privileged guidance may be misaligned with the student's functional decision because the corresponding decision can occur at a different timestep, while the student's decision itself may span multiple timesteps rather than being tied to a single timestamp. Thus, timestamp-local supervision can misalign both the context and the temporal scope of credit. To address this mismatch, we introduce AlignOPSD, following the principle of aligning supervision before assigning credit. Decision-Aligned Supervision Rectification re-scores the same student-sampled response in functionally matched contexts across sibling rollouts to calibrate local teacher evidence. Semi-Markov Hierarchical Credit Assignment then derives variable-duration decision spans from correspondence changes and uses rectified evidence to allocate outcome-grounded credit across spans and their constituent turns. We evaluate AlignOPSD with Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2.5-7B on ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA against representative baselines. AlignOPSD outperforms both GRPO and StepOPSD across all eight backbone--aggregate-metric comparisons, improving on GRPO by 5.5--8.7 \% and ranking first in six. Additional analyzes examine the two alignment stages and hyperparameter sensitivity between tasks. Our code is avaliable at https://github.com/mingju-c/Align-OPSD
